Listed on the Commodity Exchange (COMEX), a division of the CME Group, these contracts provide transparency, liquidity, and price discovery for the global gold market. Given gold’s role as a safe-haven asset, COMEX contracts often act as a barometer of investor sentiment during times of economic or geopolitical stress. Gold futures began trading on COMEX in 1974, shortly after the U.S. abandoned the gold standard in 1971. results.snippet: COMEX, short for the Commodity Exchange, is one of the primary futures and options exchanges for trading precious metals, including gold, silver, copper, and other commodities. It was established in 1933 as the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) and later merged with the Commodity Exchange Inc. (COMEX) in 1994, forming what is now known as the CME (Chicago Mercantile Exchange) Group. The climactic moment in COMEX’s history came with its merger with the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) in 1994, forming the largest physical futures trading exchange globally.
